The main result of the paper concerns the existence of harmonic maps between hyperbolic spaces. More precisely, it studies maps from \(H^m\) to \(H^n\), where \(H^m\) and \(H^n\) denote hyperbolic spaces of dimensions \(m\) and \(n\), respectively.

The setting begins with a prescribed boundary map. Let  
\[
f:\partial H^m \to \partial H^n
\]
be a Hölder continuous function between the geometric boundaries of the two hyperbolic spaces. Writing the boundary values in coordinates, this map is denoted by
\[
f=(f^1,\ldots,f^{n-1}).
\]

The paper proves that, for every \(\epsilon>0\), there exists a harmonic map
\[
u:H^m\to H^n
\]
with prescribed asymptotic boundary behavior. This harmonic map is defined in the interior of \(H^m\) and takes values in \(H^n\).

Moreover, the map \(u\) extends continuously to the boundary when the hyperbolic spaces are viewed in their Euclidean compactifications. In this Euclidean sense, \(u\) is continuous up to \(\partial H^m\).

On the boundary, the extended map assumes the prescribed values
\[
u|_{\partial H^m}=(f^1,\ldots,f^{n-1},\epsilon).
\]
Thus, the first \(n-1\) components of the boundary value are determined by the given Hölder map \(f\), while the final component is the fixed positive constant \(\epsilon\). In this way, the result establishes the existence of a harmonic extension into \(H^n\) whose boundary trace is controlled by the given Hölder data, lifted to height \(\epsilon\).

The paper is concerned with a Dirichlet-type boundary value problem for harmonic maps between hyperbolic spaces. More precisely, it studies maps from the \(m\)-dimensional hyperbolic space \(H^m\) into the \(n\)-dimensional hyperbolic space \(H^n\), where both spaces are viewed in a standard upper half-space model. In this model, the Euclidean boundary of \(H^m\) is identified with \(\partial H^m\), and the boundary at infinity of \(H^n\) can be described in terms of Euclidean boundary coordinates.

The boundary data are prescribed by a Hölder continuous map
\[
f:\partial H^m\to \partial H^n,
\]
written in coordinates as
\[
f=(f^1,\ldots,f^{n-1}).
\]
In addition, the problem includes a positive boundary height parameter \(\epsilon>0\). Instead of requiring the image of the boundary to lie exactly on \(\partial H^n\), the paper prescribes the boundary value
\[
(f^1,\ldots,f^{n-1},\epsilon),
\]
which lies at positive height \(\epsilon\) in the upper half-space model of \(H^n\). Thus the authors consider, for each fixed \(\epsilon>0\), the problem of finding a harmonic map
\[
u:H^m\to H^n
\]
which extends continuously to the Euclidean boundary of \(H^m\) and satisfies
\[
u|_{\partial H^m}=(f^1,\ldots,f^{n-1},\epsilon).
\]

The main result of the paper establishes the solvability of this boundary value problem. Namely, for every \(\epsilon>0\), there exists a harmonic map
\[
u:H^m\to H^n
\]
which is continuous up to the Euclidean boundary and whose boundary trace is precisely the prescribed map
\[
u|_{\partial H^m}=(f^1,\ldots,f^{n-1},\epsilon).
\]
This proves that Hölder boundary data on \(\partial H^m\), together with any positive height prescription \(\epsilon\), can be realized by a harmonic map into \(H^n\).

The result provides an existence theorem for harmonic maps between hyperbolic spaces with nontrivial boundary behavior. It shows that the elliptic system defining harmonic maps admits solutions under Hölder continuous boundary conditions when the target boundary values are lifted to a positive height inside the upper half-space model. In this way, the paper contributes to the analysis of harmonic maps on noncompact negatively curved manifolds and to the study of boundary value problems at infinity for maps between hyperbolic spaces.

counterfactuals.prompt: State the main theorem about existence of harmonic maps between hyperbolic spaces with prescribed Hölder boundary data, using mathematical notation.
counterfactuals.output:
**Theorem (Existence for Hölder boundary data).**  
Let \(m,n\ge 2\), and let

\[
f:\partial_\infty \mathbb H^{m}\longrightarrow \partial_\infty \mathbb H^{n}
\]

be a nonconstant Hölder-continuous map between the ideal boundaries of real hyperbolic spaces. Then there exists a harmonic map

\[
u:\mathbb H^{m}\longrightarrow \mathbb H^{n}
\]

such that \(u\) has asymptotic boundary values \(f\), i.e.

\[
\lim_{x\to \xi} u(x)=f(\xi)
\qquad \text{for every } \xi\in \partial_\infty \mathbb H^{m},
\]

where the limit is taken in the compactification

\[
\overline{\mathbb H^{n}}=\mathbb H^{n}\cup \partial_\infty \mathbb H^{n}.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
u\in C^{0}\!\left(\overline{\mathbb H^{m}},\overline{\mathbb H^{n}}\right),
\qquad
u|_{\partial_\infty \mathbb H^{m}}=f,
\]

and \(u\) satisfies the harmonic map equation

\[
\tau(u)=0
\]

on \(\mathbb H^{m}\).
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a short “main result” paragraph for a paper proving that Hölder maps between the boundaries of \(H^m\) and \(H^n\) can be extended to harmonic maps continuous up to the boundary.
counterfactuals.output:
Our main result is that boundary regularity alone suffices to solve the asymptotic Dirichlet problem for a broad class of rough boundary data. Specifically, we prove that every Hölder continuous map  
\[
f:\partial H^m \longrightarrow \partial H^n
\]
admits a harmonic extension  
\[
u:H^m\longrightarrow H^n
\]
which is continuous on the compactification \(\overline{H^m}=H^m\cup \partial H^m\) and satisfies \(u|_{\partial H^m}=f\). Thus Hölder boundary maps between ideal boundaries of real hyperbolic spaces are precisely regular enough to be realized as boundary values of harmonic maps into hyperbolic space.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Formulate a theorem: given hyperbolic spaces \(H^m\) and \(H^n\) and a Hölder boundary function \(f:\partial H^m\to\partial H^n\), show that for every \(\epsilon>0\) there exists a harmonic map \(u:H^m\to H^n\) whose boundary value is \((f,\epsilon)\).
counterfactuals.output:
**Theorem (Asymptotic Dirichlet problem for Hölder boundary data).**  
Let \(H^{m}\) and \(H^{n}\) be real hyperbolic spaces, with \(m\ge 2\), \(n\ge 2\), and let  
\[
f:\partial H^{m}\longrightarrow \partial H^{n}
\]
be a Hölder continuous map. Fix visual metrics on \(\partial H^{m}\) and \(\partial H^{n}\). Then, for every \(\epsilon>0\), there exists a harmonic map  
\[
u:H^{m}\longrightarrow H^{n}
\]
such that \(u\) has boundary value \((f,\epsilon)\) in the following sense: \(u\) extends continuously to the compactification \(H^{m}\cup \partial H^{m}\) up to an \(\epsilon\)-error on the boundary, and
\[
d_{\partial H^{n}}\bigl(u_{\infty}(\xi),f(\xi)\bigr)<\epsilon
\qquad\text{for every }\xi\in \partial H^{m},
\]
where \(u_{\infty}:\partial H^{m}\to \partial H^{n}\) denotes the boundary trace of \(u\).

Equivalently, for every geodesic ray \(\gamma:[0,\infty)\to H^{m}\) with endpoint \(\gamma(\infty)=\xi\), the image \(u(\gamma(t))\) converges, as \(t\to\infty\), to a point of \(\partial H^{n}\) lying within \(\epsilon\) of \(f(\xi)\). Thus \(u\) realizes the prescribed Hölder boundary map \(f\) at infinity up to the given error \(\epsilon\).
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Can you summarize the main result of a paper on the Dirichlet problem at infinity for harmonic maps from \(H^m\) to \(H^n\) with Hölder continuous boundary data?
counterfactuals.output:
The main result is an existence theorem for the asymptotic Dirichlet problem for harmonic maps between real hyperbolic spaces.

In the Poincaré ball models \(H^m=\mathbb B^m\) and \(H^n=\mathbb B^n\), if

\[
\phi:S^{m-1}=\partial_\infty H^m \to S^{n-1}=\partial_\infty H^n
\]

is a nonconstant Hölder continuous boundary map, then there exists a smooth harmonic map

\[
u:H^m\to H^n
\]

such that \(u\) extends continuously to the ideal boundary and

\[
u|_{\partial_\infty H^m}=\phi .
\]

Equivalently, every nonconstant Hölder continuous map between the visual boundaries of hyperbolic spaces admits a harmonic extension to the interiors.

The significance is that the boundary data are only Hölder continuous, not necessarily smooth or quasiconformal, and the result holds in arbitrary dimensions \(m,n\ge 2\). The theorem gives a positive solution to the Dirichlet problem at infinity for this class of boundary maps. The constant boundary case is excluded because a harmonic map into \(H^n\) cannot continuously take a single ideal boundary value in the usual compactification sense, except in a degenerate limiting way.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Translate this theorem into English/math prose: for hyperbolic spaces of dimensions \(m,n\), any Hölder map on the geometric boundary admits a harmonic extension into \(H^n\), continuous to the Euclidean boundary, with final coordinate \(\epsilon\).
counterfactuals.output:
**Theorem.**  
Let \(\mathbb H^{m}\) and \(\mathbb H^{n}\) be real hyperbolic spaces. Suppose  
\[
\varphi:\partial_{\infty}\mathbb H^{m}\to \partial_{\infty}\mathbb H^{n}
\]
is a Hölder-continuous map between their geometric boundaries. Then \(\varphi\) admits a harmonic extension to the interior: there exists a harmonic map  
\[
F:\mathbb H^{m}\to \mathbb H^{n}
\]
such that \(F\) extends continuously to the Euclidean/geometric boundary and satisfies  
\[
F|_{\partial_{\infty}\mathbb H^{m}}=\varphi.
\]

In the upper half-space model  
\[
\mathbb H^{n}=\{(y_{1},\dots,y_{n-1},y_{n})\in \mathbb R^{n}: y_{n}>0\},
\]
one may take the extension so that its final, or vertical, coordinate is prescribed to be  
\[
y_{n}=\epsilon>0
\]
on the relevant Euclidean boundary level. Equivalently, the harmonic extension maps into \(\mathbb H^{n}\), remains continuous up to the boundary, realizes the given boundary map \(\varphi\), and has last coordinate \(\epsilon\) at the boundary.
counterfactuals.label: cf_5
